newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker Maritime climbs on contract rumours.
newsitem.headline: Aker Maritime climbs on contract rumours.

text.p: Norwegian offshore group Aker Maritime ASA climbed strongly for the third consecutive session on Wednesday on growing market speculation that the company had won an order for the Aasgard oil and gas project.
At 1235 GMT Aker Maritime had advanced 6.50 crowns to 104.50 crowns in 25.4 million crowns of business. The stock has risen nearly 19 percent since the close on Friday at 88 crowns.
Players in the offshore sector say the operator of the Aasgard project, state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap bid any day.
The contract, estimated to be worth around seven billion crowns, is for a semi-submersible gas platform, Aasgard B, for the field which lies off mid-Norway.
Industry sources say the race for the deal apparently has narrowed to two candidates, Aker and the oil and gas division of Kvaerner ASA.
Statoil was expected to have a meeting of its board on Thursday to agree a final decision before consulting with the other licence partners in the Aasgard project.
Statoil, while refusing to comment on the rumours, says an announcement will be made at the beginning of February.
